national.line: The Orlando Eye, a 400-foot-tall observation wheel, is trying to set a new world record for Halloween - most witches on a wheel. 184 costumed witches of all ages participated on Oct. 21. Apparently brooms weren't fast enough.
A 7-week-old kitten rescued from a busy Massachusetts interstate got the perfect name - Freeway. Thankfully not Off-Ramp.
A service dog named Forest went bananas with joy when he spotted his favorite Disney character on a cruise. Even service dogs get a day off.
Peace on Earth, the Bing Crosby and David Bowie Christmas classic, only exists because Bowie didn't like the song Bing picked. Nothing says Christmas like creative differences.
Gladiator II, starring Denzel Washington and Pedro Pascal, underwhelmed in theaters at 462 million dollars but is now Netflix's number one movie. Everybody waited for it on the couch.

pride.label: Hall of Fame
pride.line: Dean Long, Lebanon High School graduate, was inducted into the Emporia State University baseball Hall of Fame in October. Not bad for a kid from Lebanon.

pride.label: National Budget Award
pride.line: Lebanon R-3 School District earned the National Meritorious Budget Award. Spreadsheets everywhere are cheering.

pride.label: Grand Opening
pride.line: Lebanon R-3 School District opened the new Robert W. Plaster Center for Student Success. Ribbon-cutting scissors got a workout.

pride.label: New Head Coach
pride.line: Brittany Stamm is the new head girls basketball coach for Lebanon Schools. Whistle shopping starts now.

pride.label: New Head Coach
pride.line: Kalem Copling is the new head boys basketball coach for Lebanon Schools. Practice just got a lot louder.

pride.label: World Food Champ Finalists
pride.line: Waynesville Career Center students Molly McDermitt, Cycila Keeney and Samantha Etheridge made the finals at the World Food Championships in Indianapolis Oct. 18 with Bacon Lover's Christmas. The judges never stood a chance.

pride.label: Teacher Award
pride.line: East Elementary teacher Kyleen Oxendine of Waynesville won the 1st Quarter Project Teach Award Oct. 19. Reading homework just got cool.

pride.label: Tiger Spirit Trophy
pride.line: Waynesville's Sixth Grade Center won the traveling Tiger Spirit Trophy again for its first-place Homecoming Parade float. That trophy isn't traveling anywhere.

pride.label: Perfect Bus Inspection
pride.line: All 10 Waynesville R-6 school buses picked at random passed a surprise Missouri State Highway Patrol inspection Oct. 20. Even the squeaky seats passed.

pride.label: Community Recognition
pride.line: Domino's of Waynesville received the school district's October Community Recognition Plaque for supporting students. Pizza: the official food of school support.

pride.label: Record Test Scores
pride.line: Bolivar School District posted its best state test scores since testing began in 1998, with 56.3 percent of students proficient in math. Somebody pass the calculators around.

pride.label: Banking School Grads
pride.line: Lathan Martin and Boone Shockley of Grand Missouri Bank in Bolivar graduated from the Oklahoma Bankers Association Consumer Lending School in Oklahoma City in October. Loan officers with diplomas to prove it.

pride.label: Perfect Inspection
pride.line: Parkview Health Care Facility in Bolivar passed its annual state inspection with zero deficiencies. Not even a dust bunny.

pride.label: 100 Years in Business
pride.line: Marshfield Chevrolet is celebrating 100 years in Marshfield. Still running better than most of us.

pride.label: Marching Band
pride.line: The Marshfield High School marching band took fourth place at the Ozark Mountain Marching Festival. Those feet never missed a step.

pride.label: Athlete of the Week
pride.line: Crocker soccer player Johnny Carriger was named KY3 Athlete of the Week for a hat trick in the district championship game, his second of the tournament. Hats are clearly his thing.

pride.label: Cross Country Title
pride.line: Macks Creek cross country teams won the title and finished runner-up at the Dixon Invitational. Running is easier when you're winning.

local.line: Lebanon street, electric, water and wastewater crews trained with two neighboring cities Oct. 21 for trench and confined space rescues. Hopefully the only trench drama all year.
Lebanon R-3 School District's Hive Depot is giving Lebanon students essential resources and learning opportunities. Busy bees, indeed.
A historic Route 66 gas station in Marshfield has been restored. Fill-ups not included.
A retro Route 66 diner in St. Robert is getting attention as the Missouri road-trip stop for chicken-fried steak and malts. Pants with stretch recommended.
Webster County Health Unit officially launched its Baby Bridge program for families with babies and toddlers after a two-month pilot. Toddlers approve, probably.
Two new Missouri State Highway Patrol troopers have joined the Lake of the Ozarks area. Maybe ease off the gas a bit.
The Polk County Museum hosted homeschoolers learning Cherokee history and customs. Best field trip of the semester.
Seymour's estimated population is now 2,247. Everybody wave.

music.line: Ella Langley sang a fiery version of Dolly Parton's 1974 hit Jolene at the CMA's I Will Always Love You tribute to Dolly. Jolene, consider yourself warned.
Reba McEntire sang He's Alive with the Belmont University choir to honor her longtime friend Dolly Parton and got a standing ovation. Reba gets those a lot.
Zac Brown sang Butterfly alongside Dolly Parton's own recorded vocals at the CMA tribute to Dolly. A duet across time.
Kelsea Ballerini sang Dolly Parton's Here You Come Again at the CMA tribute and ended with, We love you, Miss Dolly. Everybody does.
Brad Paisley and Sierra Hull sang Dolly Parton's When I Get Where I'm Going at the CMA tribute. Bring tissues for this one.
The Country Music Association is giving one million dollars to Dolly Parton's Imagination Library. That's a lot of bedtime stories.
Zach Top is bringing his sold-out Red Rocks shows to drive-in theaters as a concert film. Pass the popcorn and the cowboy hat.
Kacey Musgraves announced Middle of Nowhere Volume 2: Tex Mex Tapes and previewed two new songs, Weekend in Texas and Mi Tesoro. Queso not included.
Lainey Wilson and Marty Stuart unveiled a Wildflowers and Wild Horses mural in downtown Philadelphia, Mississippi. Bell-bottoms in paint form.
Ella Langley cast singer Kaitlin Butts as the mean girl in her Choosin' Texas video because she knew Butts would nail it. Acting range, unlocked.
Tim McGraw, Paul Overstreet and the Stanley Brothers are the newest members of the Country Music Hall of Fame in Nashville. Clear some wall space.
Kip Moore released The Wolf, a new song for the Prime Video series The Terminal List. Howl along.
John Osborne says a childhood bully inspired the Brothers Osborne song Tough Kid. Revenge is a hit single.
Morgan Wallen's Sand in My Boots festival returns to Gulf Shores, Alabama, in 2027 after a year off. Pack the sunscreen early.
Chris Stapleton's You Should Probably Leave just passed one billion Spotify streams, his second song to do it. Nobody's leaving yet.

Zach Bryan, who just turned 30 and reportedly sold his song catalog for 350 million dollars, released an eight-song EP, Young Manhood and Other Donatable Organs, to go with a book about his life. That title is a mouthful.
Jordan Davis' new radio single is called Mess, and he told Billboard the melody locked him in right away. Best mess he ever made.
Luke Combs extended his record with his 23rd straight number one on country radio, Be By You. At this point, just give him the chart.
Bo Bryan, Luke Bryan's son and a 2027 quarterback recruit, got a scholarship offer from the University of Georgia. Dad's tailgate plans are set.
Riley Green says he wants to be a dad and pictures camo, hunting trips and plenty of new songs. Baby's first tree stand.
Cole Swindell turned family memories into his new single, Bronco. Every family has a Bronco story.
Brooks and Dunn played a surprise Nashville show to celebrate 35 years of their Brand New Man album. Not so brand new anymore.
Emily Ann Roberts launches her first headlining run, The Thread Tour, hitting 23 cities in spring 2027. Sew far, sew good.
CMA Presents I Will Always Love You, a two-hour Dolly Parton tribute special starring country's biggest names, is coming to TV. Clear the DVR.
Little Big Town, HARDY and the Red Clay Strays lead New Year's Eve Live: Nashville's Big Bash Dec. 31 on CBS and Paramount Plus. Staying up till midnight just got easier.
Blake Shelton, Rascal Flatts and Brad Paisley will headline VOA Fest 2026. That's a lot of cowboy hats.
Emmy-winning duo The War and Treaty will get the first-ever Origins Vanguard Award at the 2026 Origins Impact Awards. Clear a spot on the shelf.
Zach Top is adding more shows to his Cold Beer and Country Music Tour. The title says it all.
On this day in 2023, Luke Combs hit number one with a cover song that helped a folk legend make country music history. Good covers never go out of style.
Brothers Osborne have a new album, Watertown, on the way. Stay hydrated, folks.

weird.line: Santa Cruz, California, rounded up a loose emu on city streets, just days after a different emu got out there. Somebody check the emu gate.
A ghostly white raccoon in Florida got caught on camera raiding a cat's dinner. The cat was not consulted.
A black bear wandered into a family's backyard and swiped a drink out of their fridge, and the homeowner said, I figured he was thirsty. Hospitality, Southern style.
A 3,156-pound pumpkin grown in Rhode Island is being inspected as a possible world record. That's a lot of pie.
A 2,455-pound pumpkin set a new record at an Ohio pumpkin show. Cinderella's ride just got an upgrade.
Aspinwall, Pennsylvania's pumpkin guy carved a record-breaking 1,906-pound pumpkin for charity. Bring a bigger knife.
Susan Burgos of California set a Guinness World Record with 13,201 frog collectibles. Her house must be ribbiting.
Pennsylvania has a new state record channel catfish, the first time that record has fallen in 35 years. The fish story finally came true.
Neighbors in a Tennessee town are watching for a pet kangaroo that escaped. It's probably hopping mad.
Sammy the pig, who escaped during a music festival in Gautier, Mississippi, was found after days on the run. Guess he wasn't a fan of the opener.
A cow got loose and went wandering on a Maryland highway. Moo-ving violation.
Georgia firefighters rescued a chameleon stuck on a high branch. Hard to find a rescue that blends in.
An Oklahoma sheriff's office finally caught a caiman, a small alligator cousin, after months on the loose, and the body camera got it all. See you later, caiman.
A Maryland man left a Mega Millions ticket in his car's sun visor for weeks, then found out it won 30,000 dollars. Time to clean out the car.
Western wear brand Tecovas now holds the world record for the largest hat. Hat hair for days.
A meteorite hunter found a 1,430-pound space rock buried under a Kansas farm in 2005. Best rock that farm ever grew.
Scientists discovered a new squid-like species in Wyoming that lived 160 million years ago. Wyoming used to be beachfront.
A 4-year-old boy's reaction to hearing his parents' voices for the very first time has gone viral. Grab the tissues.
A dog owner dressed up as a giant raccoon, and the dogs' reactions went viral. Those dogs need therapy now.
A YouTuber turned Linkin Park's In the End into LinkedIn Park, a workplace anthem made of corporate jargon. Let's circle back on that.
A popular marble racing channel held a Halloween race through a haunted castle full of giant hungry spiders. Some of those marbles lost their marbles.

humor.line: It isn't actually a pie but a cake, first whipped up in 1856 by a French chef at Boston's Parker House Hotel. Nobody tell the pie.
It's about chemistry, not the critter, and it runs from 6:02 in the morning to 6:02 at night to honor Avogadro's number, 6.02 times ten to the 23rd. The nerdiest clock-in ever.
A fan made the day up, and in 2018 Crocs released a limited-edition gold-foiled clog for it that sold out within hours. Fancy Crocs, the height of fashion.
In 1795, France offered a 12,000-franc prize for a way to preserve food, and chef Nicolas Appert came up with heating it and sealing it in airtight glass jars. Grandma's pantry owes him big.
It falls on Johnny Carson's birthday, the King of Late Night who hosted The Tonight Show from 1962 until 1992. Heeere's Johnny.
One famous kind is Lebanon bologna, though it comes from Lebanon, Pennsylvania, where two companies have made it since the late 1800s. Sorry, Lebanon, Missouri.
Those pink and white candy-coated licorice pieces are the oldest candy brand made in the United States, first produced in Philadelphia in 1893. Still the movie candy nobody shares.
It's promoted by a tongue-in-cheek website called the Tripe Marketing Board, and the date comes from a 1662 diary entry where Samuel Pepys raved about a dish of tripe. One fan, 364 years later.
It marks the day in 1938 when the law creating the 40-hour work week took effect, and that same law set the minimum wage at 25 cents. Ask for that raise.
It started in 1975 as an Earth Day for food, and when it came back in 2011, more than 2,300 events were held across the country. Everybody brought a casserole.
The whole idea is to break your normal routine and do things a little differently, and it counts as a success if you make somebody laugh. So, a normal Friday.
A Michigan man created it to honor his old roommate on his birthday, and the roommate's last name was Sauer. Some friendships come with a pucker.
The official advice for celebrating: when in doubt, just deep fry any food you have. Doctors hate this one trick.
Pizza started in Naples in the late 1700s as cheap flatbread for working people, back when Naples was its own kingdom and not part of Italy. A kingdom built on crust.
Holidays for mothers-in-law go back to at least the early 1920s, but it didn't land on the fourth Sunday in October until the mid-1970s. Call her. Seriously.
It started at the first World Pasta Congress in Rome in 1995, where countries agreed to team up and get the whole world eating more pasta. Best treaty ever signed.
You're supposed to dress up like a punk rocker and crank up punk music, the sound born in the 1970s with bands like the Ramones. Mohawk optional.
It marks 1785, when the King of Spain sent two donkeys to the United States as a gift, and George Washington used them to breed the first mules of their kind in the country. Stubborn, but loyal.

A Dallas PR man got turned down by both the state agriculture department and the Texas Beef Council before a state lawmaker who was also in the restaurant business took up his cause. Persistence, with gravy.
The word pumpkin comes from the Greek word pepon, which means large melon. Pumpkin spice melon latte, anyone?
Mincemeat traditionally mixes minced meat, fat and fruit, but many modern recipes leave the meat out entirely. So it's just mince now.
The date comes from a 1769 diary entry about writer Samuel Johnson being told of a newly invented machine that drove without horses. The horses were thrilled.
You're supposed to let your cranky co-workers complain all they want today instead of trying to cheer them up. You know who you are.
Potatoes were first grown thousands of years ago in what is now Peru and Bolivia, and Scotch-Irish immigrants brought them to New Hampshire in 1719. Couch potatoes came later.
It was set up in 1922 and falls on Teddy Roosevelt's birthday. Speak softly and carry a big boat.
There are 22 types of black cats, and many places waive black cat adoption fees on Black Friday. Best Black Friday deal going.
The word chocolate traces back to the Aztec word xocolatl, which means bitter water. Thank goodness for sugar.
The statue arrived in New York in 1885 packed in 214 crates and had to be put back together before it was dedicated in 1886. Some assembly required.
It likely caught on thanks to Euell Gibbons, whose 1962 book was called Stalking the Wild Asparagus. The asparagus never saw it coming.
It honors the first public showing of projected moving pictures, Emile Reynaud's Theatre Optique, in 1892. Saturday morning cartoons started somewhere.
You're encouraged to take your stuffed animals out of storage and bring them everywhere you go for the day. Teddy's riding shotgun.
It was created by Colleen Paige, who also founded National Dog Day, and cats live in more than a third of American homes. The cats will pretend not to care.
It marks 1969, when the very first electronic message was sent from one computer to another over ARPANET, the network that came before the internet. Probably asked to reply-all.
Oatmeal starts as hulled oats called groats, which get heated to give them their nutty flavor. Groats: a fun word to say.
